subject: general
question: Which feature of the phosphodiester bond contributes most to the overall negative charge of the DNA molecule?

options.text: The phosphate group’s ionisable oxygen atoms

solution:
The correct answer is __**The phosphate group's ionisable oxygen atoms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• DNA molecules carry a** negative charge**, primarily due to the presence of the phosphate group in the phosphodiester backbone.
 
• The phosphate group contains **ionisable oxygen atoms** that are negatively charged at physiological pH.
 
• These negatively charged oxygen atoms contribute to the **overall negative charge of the DNA molecule**, which affects its interactions with proteins, cations, and other molecules.
 
• The negative charge of DNA is critical for its **structural stability and biological functions**, such as in its interaction with histones and its electrophoretic mobility during gel-based experiments.
 
• Other components of DNA, such as the nitrogenous bases and the sugar, do not contribute significantly to the molecule's overall charge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phosphodiester Bond:**

 
 
• A phosphodiester bond is a chemical bond formed between the 3'-hydroxyl group of one sugar and the phosphate group attached to the 5'-carbon of another sugar in the DNA or RNA backbone.
 
• This bond is crucial for the formation of the DNA and RNA polymer structure.
 
 
 
• **Role of Negative Charge in DNA:**
 
 
• The negative charge on DNA facilitates its interaction with positively charged proteins such as histones, which help in DNA packaging in chromatin.
 
• It also allows the DNA to migrate towards the positive electrode during electrophoresis, a common laboratory technique for DNA analysis.
 
 
 
• **Physiological pH:**
 
 
• The ionisation of the phosphate group occurs at physiological pH (~7.4), ensuring the DNA remains negatively charged under normal biological conditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Components of DNA:**
 
 
• The nitrogenous bases (adenine, thymine, cytosine, guanine) and the deoxyribose sugar are neutral and do not contribute to the overall charge of the DNA molecule.
